sessions.feedback: No news or deal-status tool made INSM's deal inference (a pinned price on 79M shares) a guess from price alone. A tool that returns the previous day's open-high-low-close range and volume for a held name inside get_quotes would help. The digest's pre-market list covers only the top 20 by sd and is dominated by thin prints, so a filter on a minimum share of average-day volume would make it more useful.

Without news access I can't tell whether a +14.6% pre-market surge on 12.5M shares (INSM) is a buyout, where the price pins, or a data or approval event, where it drifts. A headline field in the digest, or even a flag for "halted/news pending" would help. The scan tool does not say whether a stock reports earnings today or yesterday, so the earnings-gap logic has to be inferred. An earnings calendar flag would improve gap-drift trade selection. The 'extend' action is ambiguous about the reference price for stops and targets when no fill happens (I assumed the open).

No news access made it impossible to tell whether the big pre-market gaps (KYMR +30% at a round 150.00, ZS +20%, CRWD -7% against the market, UNH -6%) were data, earnings or a buyout. A short headline field for each name in the pre-market movers list would remove most of the coin-flip skips. Also, the digest's top-20 list is ranked by sd and includes many 100-share prints. A minimum-volume filter on that list would show more tradeable names.

No problems this session. The digest's top-gainers list showed only one stock (INSM), so I had little to scan on the long side. A fuller movers list with market cap and volume as a multiple of the 20-day median would help. The scan's 'vol x avg' understated the INSM spike because the average includes an earlier spike (14.4M shares showed as 3.9x).

Nothing blocked me this session. The main limit is that I can't tell whether a gap is earnings, an offering or news, and that decides whether the drift trade makes sense. An earnings-date flag in scan or search_symbols (days since or until earnings, and the EPS surprise sign) would help a lot without needing a news feed. The pre-market ranking by sd is dominated by thin prints, so a volume filter such as at least 5% of an average day would be useful.

A way to see whether a pre-market gap comes from earnings would help a lot, for example an earnings-date calendar or an 'earnings today' flag in the digest or scan. Without it I can't tell an earnings gap from an offering or a rumor. That is why I skipped ARDT, GLBE and TTWO and took TJX with moderate conviction. The pre-market list also shows many thin prints (a few hundred shares) near the top, which crowds out real movers. A minimum share count filter would help.

No news access made unusual pre-market movers (SLS +308%, AS +4.8%, TU last session) impossible to judge, so I skipped them. A headline or catalyst-type field in the digest, even just earnings versus non-earnings, would let price/volume analysis separate earnings drift from random spikes. It would also help to see the original entry fill date and horizon status in the digest for the extend decisions.
Nothing blocking. Having no news makes gap-drift trades unverifiable, but that is the stated design.

- AMBA (-34% pre-market, $1.2B cap), NTNX (-14%) and URBN (-11%): shorting after a gap with unknown cause is a coin flip (rule 3).
- EMBC (+40%) and CD: tiny caps.
- Shorting the semis crash: continuation versus a violent bounce is a coin flip.

Cash is about 62% after closing INSM.

Notes (2026-11-25): Strategy is price/volume only, no news access. Open trades: GKOS (entry 228.57) and CROX (entry 145.06), post-earnings-gap drift trades opened 10/29, CROX horizon ends 12/2. TJX (entry 137.15, 11/18), PDD (entry 82.46, 11/19), DKS (148.90, 11/24 +16% gap), SNY (50.38, 11/24 +6.6% gap). Closed: ZS (bought 11/23 on a +20% pre-market gap, stopped at -8.2% the same day, so the gap faded). INSM closed 11/25 (a deal).

Market state: violent regime. SPY 11/19 -1.96%, 11/20 -3.64%, 11/23 +4.71%, 11/24 -0.49%, 11/25 pre-market -1.9% (QQQ -2.9%). The AI/semis complex is crashing: NVDA -23.6% over 20d, MU -11% on 11/24 and -6.6% pre-market 11/25, SNDK, AMD, INTC all -6 to -11%. Rotation into healthcare and staples (XLV +3% on 11/24). My book is deliberately non-tech. Thanksgiving 11/26 (closed), 11/27 half day.

Rules of thumb:
(1) Don't chase pre-market spikes in thin small caps without news (SLS 11/17, 308% pre-market).
(2) The gap setup I trust is a gap on 3x+ volume after a decline, in a stock with a real market cap. Slippage there is 0.1-0.25%. Check that the gap is stock-specific against peers (TJX 11/18: HD/LOW down. PDD 11/19: BABA/JD/BIDU flat to down. DKS 11/24: NKE/ONON/DECK flat. SNY 11/24: AZN +1.1%, but the whole health sector was +3% that day, so the idiosyncratic part was about +7%).
(3) Shorting after a -6% to -20% gap with an unknown cause is a coin flip, so skip unless the pattern is clear (skipped ARDT, GLBE, NTES, WSM, INTU, ROST, UNH, ADI -13%, SHOE -22%, AMBA -34% pre-market 11/25, NTNX -14%, URBN -11%).
(4) Sector-wide surges (cybersecurity 11/18) are not stock-specific signals. Don't chase the leader after a 2-day +20% move.
(5) Pre-market counts shown in the digest are thin. Use 'shares as % of avg day' above about 10% as a minimum for believing a gap.
(6) The scan's 'vol x avg' can understate a spike when the 60-day average already includes an earlier spike (INSM). Check raw volume in get_history.
(7) Relative strength on a big down market day (stock up while SPY -2%) is a useful stock-specific signal: PDD 11/19, INSM 11/19, CROX/GKOS 11/16, TJX 11/20.
(8) A pre-market print at a round number (KYMR 150.00, +30%) can mean a buyout, where there's no alpha.
(9) Gap-drift trades opened 10/29 to 11/24 (CROX, GKOS, TJX, PDD, INSM, DKS, SNY) are all positive vs cost. But ZS 11/23 (+20% pre-market gap on a violent bounce day, 30% of avg volume) hit its -8% stop the same day. Size 4-5%, stop 8-9%.
(10) When a held name gaps through its target pre-market (INSM 11/24), act explicitly: trim and re-set stop/target from the new fill.
(11) Retail earnings week (11/18 TJX, 11/24 DKS/ANF/BURL/BBY gaps up, SHOE gap down): read-across inside the group. I avoid stacking more than 2 new names in one industry.
(12) Deal detector (INSM 11/24-25): a day on very heavy volume (79M shares, 36% of shares outstanding) with an open-to-close range under 0.5% and a flat pre-market the next day while SPY moves 2% is a cash deal. Close it. It had given +19% vs cost in 5 sessions after the first gap on 11/19 (20% surge on 14M shares, then 11/24 deal).
(13) Trailing stops: after a gap trade has held for a week, put the stop just under the post-gap lows (use get_history lows). Use extend, which measures stop/target from today's fill.

Open questions: Does SNY (pre-market 53.60) hold above 50.3? Does DKS hold above 150 (pre-market 153.3)? Do CROX (horizon 12/2, stop 146.91), GKOS (stop 231.25), TJX, PDD (stop 81.42) hold? CROX has been range-bound 150-164 for 4 weeks on falling volume, so the drift is probably over: close it at the 12/2 horizon unless it breaks 164 on volume.
